paper: Gonzalez-Escalona et al. 2019, PLoS ONE 14(7):e0220494 -- Nanopore sequencing for fast determination of plasmids, phages, virulence markers, and AMR genes in STEC O26:H11
verdict_context: PARTIAL (downstream biology replicates; cross-platform MinION-vs-MiSeq-vs-PacBio de novo assembly comparison not re-executed)

open_questions.q: At current Oxford Nanopore R10.4.1 chemistry (Q20+ raw-read accuracy, duplex reads) and modern assemblers (Flye/Trycycler/Medaka polishing), do MinION-only STEC assemblies still miss any of the plasmid or chromosome virulence loci (toxB, tccP, iha, astA) that the 2019 R9.4 + Canu v1.6 pipeline could recover only with PacBio backup, or is nanopore now fully sufficient as a standalone platform for closing STEC genomes?
open_questions.basis: The paper's central methodological claim (2019) was that MinION R9.4 + Canu v1.6 assemblies were congruent with PacBio HGAP3+Quiver, but the raw-reads comparison was not re-executed in this replication (see C9/C10, deferred). Since 2019, nanopore chemistry has advanced two full generations (R9.4 -> R10.3 -> R10.4.1) and per-read accuracy has moved from ~92-95% to >99% (Q20+) with duplex; single-platform sufficiency needs re-benchmarking against the same three isolates.
open_questions.next_steps: Re-sequence CFSAN027343/346/350 on a MinION R10.4.1 flow cell (or use one of the public 2024+ STEC R10 datasets); assemble with Flye + Medaka + Trycycler; run the same AMRFinderPlus + CGE screens as this replication; compute per-gene recall vs the PacBio reference (CP037941-CP037947). Target: does R10.4.1-only recover 6/6 AMR genes on the 72 kb plasmid and 6/6 Table 7 discriminating virulence genes without hybrid short-read polishing?

open_questions.q: For AMR gene detection specifically, how much value does hybrid short+long-read assembly (Unicycler / hybridSPAdes) still add over long-read-only assembly at modern nanopore chemistry, and does the answer depend on plasmid copy number or repeat content around the AMR cassette?
open_questions.basis: This paper found the 6 acquired AMR genes only on the 72 kb IncFII plasmid in strain 346, and its authors implicitly relied on long-read scaffolds to place them on that plasmid rather than in scattered short-read contigs -- but did not benchmark hybrid assembly. Current field practice (2024-2026) has increasingly moved to long-read-only, but hybrid may still matter for low-copy plasmids or IS-element-rich regions.
open_questions.next_steps: Using the three CFSAN027 strains: (a) MiSeq-only SPAdes assembly of SRR8333590-92; (b) MinION-only Flye assembly of SRR8335317-18 (upgrade to R10 if possible); (c) hybrid Unicycler; and (d) hybrid Trycycler + short-read polish. Compare per-assembly AMR-gene recall and correct plasmid placement (contig contiguity) against the CP037947 reference. Stratify by plasmid replicon type (IncFII vs IncFIB) and by IS-density flanking each AMR gene.

open_questions.q: What is the achievable end-to-end latency (sample-in to actionable serotype+MLST+AMR report) for a real-time nanopore-based STEC public-health surveillance workflow in 2026, and is it fast enough to intervene in an active outbreak before secondary transmission?
open_questions.basis: The paper positions MinION as 'accurate and economical' but reports only assembly-level metrics, not clock-time-to-report. STEC outbreaks (particularly O26:H11 and O157:H7) have doubling times measured in days, so latency between sample receipt and typed report is the operationally binding variable. This is not addressed in the paper.
open_questions.next_steps: Build a documented, time-stamped protocol: DNA extraction -> R10.4.1 rapid barcoding -> MinION sequencing (target 30x per isolate) -> real-time basecalling (Dorado) -> streaming assembly (Flye) -> AMRFinderPlus + mlst + serotype call. Instrument each stage. Publish the wall-clock budget per stage for a batch of 12 outbreak isolates on a MinION Mk1C (field-portable) vs GridION (benchtop). Compare to the paper's implied 'a few days' turnaround with the 2019 workflow.

open_questions.q: At outbreak-relevant coverage (10-30x rather than the >100x used by the paper's PacBio references), what is the SNP-resolution limit of nanopore-only assemblies for distinguishing closely related STEC isolates within a single outbreak, and does it match the resolution needed for cgMLST or wgSNP epidemiological trees?
open_questions.basis: The paper uses very high PacBio coverage on 3 archival isolates and does not benchmark low-coverage outbreak-mode use. Downstream users of the method (public-health labs) typically operate at much lower per-isolate coverage to sequence many isolates per flow cell, and cgMLST/wgSNP-tree resolution at that coverage is not established for STEC O26:H11 in this paper.
open_questions.next_steps: Subsample the paper's own reads (or new R10.4.1 reads on the same strains) to 10x, 20x, 30x, 50x, 100x; assemble each subsample with Flye+Medaka; compute pairwise SNP distance between the two ST21 strains (343 vs 346) at each coverage using snippy/parsnp against the CP037945 chromosome reference; determine the coverage floor below which the pairwise SNP distance ceases to be within the accepted +/-5 SNP outbreak-cluster window. Cross-check against short-read wgSNP as ground truth.

open_questions.q: What is the current (2026) real cost-per-isolate and throughput-per-hour of a MinION Mk1C field-portable workflow for STEC typing (including consumables, labor, and cloud/compute for basecalling+assembly), and how does that compare on a per-isolate basis to (a) short-read MiSeq typing and (b) shipping isolates to a centralized reference lab?
open_questions.basis: The paper's 2019 cost/throughput claim -- MinION as 'economical' -- was made against 2019 nanopore chemistry, flow-cell prices, and pre-Mk1C hardware. Flow cell prices, wash-kit reuse, and integrated compute (Mk1C basecalls onboard) have all shifted. No current published cost-per-isolate figure exists for STEC-specific workflows in this paper.
open_questions.next_steps: Assemble a itemized cost model for three scenarios on a 12-isolate outbreak batch: (1) MinION Mk1C field-portable (rapid barcoding kit + one R10.4.1 flow cell + onboard basecalling + Flye+AMRFinderPlus); (2) benchtop MiSeq v3 600-cycle + Nextera XT + SPAdes; (3) ship to CDC/PulseNet reference lab. Report cost per isolate, wall-clock to report, and require operator FTE-hours. Sensitivity-analyze against flow-cell reuse (wash kit) and multiplexing depth.
